name: SPARCS Ambulatory Surgery Encounters by Facility: Beginning 2018
description: This dataset is a summary of the ambulatory surgery encounters reported in SPARCS data, summarized by facility and quarter of visit.

Dataset Summary.Program Owner: Center for Applied Research and Evaluation
Dataset Summary.Office/Division: Office of Health Services Quality and Analytics

Disclaimers.Limitations: SPARCS data is continually submitted and updated and facility submission timeframes may vary.  The counts reflected in this dataset are subject to change as the data matures.  Facility name, operator, and type reflect current attributes at the time the data was compiled and might not reflect historical facility type or affiliations. Ambulatory surgery encounters are defined by revenue code reporting and do not necessarily reflect  ambulatory surgery certification on the facility operating certificates. Facilities with less than 10 ambulatory surgery encounters reported within a calendar year are removed.

Notes.Notes: Statewide Planning and Research Cooperative System (SPARCS) is a comprehensive all payer data reporting system established in 1979 as a result of cooperation between the healthcare industry and government. The system was initially created to collect information on discharges from hospitals. SPARCS currently collects patient-level detail on patient characteristics, diagnoses and treatments, services, and charges for each hospital inpatient stay and outpatient (ambulatory surgery, emergency department, and outpatient services) visit; and each ambulatory surgery and outpatient services visit to a hospital extension clinic and diagnostic and treatment center licensed to provide ambulatory surgery services.

name: Temporary Elevator Mechanics License
description: The dataset includes a comprehensive list of temporary elevator mechanics licenses that have been issued to individuals for the purpose of performing elevator work during a verifiable shortage of licensed mechanics. The dataset includes the individual’s name and license information, such as license number, license type, issue date, expiration date, and status.

Dataset Summary.Time Period: Current - The data includes all active licenses and licenses that have expired within the last year. The license is active for 90 days as long as the temporary elevator mechanic is employed by the licensed elevator contractor.
Dataset Summary.Dataset Owner: New York State Department of Labor

Disclaimers.Limitations: Licenses that have expired over a year ago will not be available in the dataset.

name: RSV Hospitalizations: Beginning October 2025
description: This dataset includes weekly aggregate counts of persons hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed RSV, by county beginning with the 2025-26 season. The primary goal of this dataset is to provide timely information about RSV-associated hospitalizations throughout the respiratory season. Although each respiratory season is unique, historical data is provided for trend comparison.

Dataset Summary.Office/Division: Division of Epidemiology, Center for Community Health, Office of Public Health

Notes.Notes: Data are posted weekly during the season (MMWR week 40-week 39 of the next year; October-September)

name: RSV Laboratory Confirmed Cases by County: Beginning October 2025
description: This dataset includes weekly counts of persons with laboratory-confirmed Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), by county and virus type, beginning with the 2025-2026 season. The primary goal of this dataset is to provide timely information about RSV virus activity throughout the respiratory season. Although each season is unique, historical data is also provided for trend comparison.

Dataset Summary.Program Owner: Division of Epidemiology Bureau of Communicable Disease Control and Bureau of Surveillance and Disease Systems
Dataset Summary.Time Period: Beginning with the 2025-2026 Respiratory Virus Season (October 2025 onward)
Dataset Summary.Office/Division: Division of Epidemiology, Center for Community Health, Office of Public Health

Disclaimers.Limitations: These data are an undercount of the true number of RSV cases because they only represent illnesses where 1) an ill patient seeks medical care, 2) an appropriate specimen is collected for diagnostic testing, 3) such testing is performed in a clinical laboratory that reports results to ECLRS, and 4) test results are positive. It is unknown how many patients do not seek medical care, are not tested by a reliable assay, or are tested in settings that do not report results to ECLRS. Further, certain tests such as RDTs have limited accuracy; false negative and false positive results do occur. The number of laboratories reporting data to ECLRS has increased over time. However, it is not known how RSV virus testing practices or the proportion of all tests being performed in clinical laboratory settings have changed over time or how they vary geographically. Thus, caution should be used when comparing data such as absolute numbers of cases between seasons or counties. Despite these limitations, the data can provide useful situational awareness (e.g., trend) information during a respiratory virus season. Data may also be used to compare epidemic characteristics, e.g., timing or proportion of virus types, between seasons. However, comparing absolute numbers of cases between seasons should be approached with caution, as noted above.

Notes.Notes: Data are posted weekly during the season, beginning with the 2025-2026 season (MMWR weeks 40-week 39 of the next year; October-September)
